mechanism: Per-object instance-file close on GC never reaches the real run unit: ~CobolObject enqueues the close via RunUnit.Current, which is AsyncLocal-backed, so on the finalizer thread it creates an orphan RunUnit and the owning registry never drains the close; an unreachable object's file stays open (and registered) until run-unit end
repro: /tmp/adj/refute/gc2.cob (copied to adjudication/adj-a1-w1-s4/probes/): loop creates an object that opens its own file OUTPUT and writes without CLOSE, drops the reference, forces allocation; next object's OPEN OUTPUT -> 'K=00000002 OPEN-OUTPUT=61' (re-confirmed by the adjudicator at pin). gc1.cob: record never flushed after ~4M allocations (READ=10).
expected_from_spec: §9.3.14.3: an instance object is destroyed when it is determined it cannot take part in continued execution; §9.1.4: implicit CLOSE of the object's file connectors when the object is deleted
observed_or_reasoning: the GC does determine unreachability and runs the finalizer, but the close lands on an orphan RunUnit (RunUnit.Current => _current.Value ??= new RunUnit()); only CobolFile.CloseAll at run-unit termination closes the file
owning_note: NONE (new) — sweep other finalizer/thread-pool callers of RunUnit.Current
